title: fix(cli): reject non-executable explicit binary paths
body:
AI-assisted.

Supersedes #146988 by @Alix-007. The three contributor commits are retained with their authorship; this branch adds one test-ordering commit.

## What Problem This Solves

A configured directory or non-executable file was reported available, so iMessage setup skipped the command-path correction. Explicit paths now use the shared executable-file predicate without lexical normalization or a new cache.

## User Impact

Directories and mode-0644 files now show the CLI-path guidance and `imsg CLI path` field. Executable files and valid symlink-parent paths retain `iMessage next steps`; trailing `/` still requests correction. No config key, schema, protocol, dependency, or stored format changes.

Saved paths remain intact until the user completes setup. Cancelling leaves configuration unchanged; the next setup or preflight checks the path again. The existing input validator is unchanged, so this repair offers correction rather than guaranteeing that an entered replacement can launch.

## Test correction

Local validation found that the contributor's positive controls warm native macOS execute-access lookup before the invalid-traversal assertion. The takeover preserves all contributor commits and every assertion, checking rejection before those controls. It changes no production code. A standalone C probe reproduces the native lookup transition after successful execute access; its internal cause was not traced. Checking fresh invalid fixtures first preserves every assertion and still fails an intentionally incorrect lexical-normalization variant. The traversal tests do not claim order-independent rejection after earlier native checks.

## Evidence

- Real terminal and Gateway setup: red on main `2c393ecf556304af959b25e7ccb38c0c875be353`, green on the contributor's unchanged production code. Sanitized receipts: `red/`, `green/cli-directory-tty.log`, and the five `green/*-gateway.json` scenario receipts.
- Fresh merge `a7827c8c54ca42a1566bcd85b6768b84e4ba3598` joins the takeover head with main `a7344f3d03551ef930bbdbbf180209950352581a`. Owner and setup-sibling suites: **48 passed, 2 platform skips**. Receipts: `identities.json`, `final-owner-sibling-tests.log` and its command/exit receipt.
- Changed-file lint, formatting, line-limit and assertion checks pass. All 25 permitted selected core/structural checks pass; routing-owner assertions add **153 passes**. Receipts: `final-oxlint`, `final-oxfmt`, `final-line-ratchet`, `final-assertion-ratchet`, and `routing-tests` logs.
- Retained [published Linux/Windows evidence](https://github.com/Alix-007/openclaw/actions/runs/34763879990): **24 Linux and 15 Windows observations**, including integrity/non-execution controls. It applies to the unchanged production files; it is not a fresh native run of the test-only correction.
- [CI run 34797738230](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34797738230) passed at `c4ca622705f4d0ca95c3ec03458f789ed1712e62`. No typecheck or full build ran locally. Native lookup observations establish fresh-fixture behavior, not guaranteed later execution.

## Consumers

- iMessage setup, status and RPC preflight adopt the stricter explicit-path result.
- Signal managed-native setup adopts it; remote transports retain their own paths.
- Bare-command browser, onboarding, Raft and companion-call probes are unchanged.
- Existing executable resolvers keep the same predicate. Public setup exports keep their signatures. No new state writer or invalidation rule is introduced.

## Compatibility

Explicit-path detection adopts the existing shared executable-file predicate in `src/infra/executable-path.ts`, including its Windows `PATHEXT` rule, as explicitly accepted by the owner. Native suffixes and extensionless regular files remain accepted; other suffixes must appear in `PATHEXT`. A previously accepted custom suffix can now receive missing-binary guidance. This is availability policy, not a guarantee of launch success.
